med-spa-aesthetics.name: Med spas and aesthetics
med-spa-aesthetics.alt: An aesthetic injector examining a client's face in a medical spa treatment room
med-spa-aesthetics.h1: Marketing for med spas and aesthetic practices
med-spa-aesthetics.lead: Your patients choose you with their eyes first, pay out of pocket, and decide whether to return every few months. Marketing for an aesthetic practice has to win the first visit and earn the next one.

challenges.d: When every practice in town advertises a per-unit special, patients learn to shop by discount and leave for the next one. Your marketing has to show who is holding the syringe and why that matters, so you are chosen for trust and not for the lowest offer.

Most of the value of an aesthetic patient comes from the visits after the first, yet many practices spend everything on new leads and nothing on bringing people back. Without reminders, memberships and follow-up, patients drift to whoever shows up in their feed next.

Aesthetic patients message at night from Instagram, a web form or a text, and they often contact several practices at once. If your front desk replies the next afternoon, the consultation has usually been booked somewhere else.

plan.d: In the first weeks we review your site, profiles, reviews, ads and how inquiries are handled today, and we talk with your providers and front desk. We agree on the treatments that matter most to the practice.

Next we publish new pages, film the first round of short videos with your providers and start campaigns for your priority treatments. Text and e-mail follow-up for existing patients goes live.
By day 90 we sit down with you to review which channels produced calls and bookings and which did not. We shift effort toward what is working and set the plan for the following quarter.

dermatology.h1: Marketing for dermatology practices, medical and cosmetic

A patient worried about a changing mole and a patient comparing cosmetic injectors want very different things from the same site. If the two are mixed together, medical patients doubt the seriousness and cosmetic patients go to a med spa down the street.

Most people type a symptom or a diagnosis, not the word dermatologist. A practice with one general services page is hard to find for acne, eczema, psoriasis, hair loss, rosacea and the many other conditions it treats every day.

care: Claims about what hormone therapy, peptides or IV therapy can do must be accurate and supportable, and words such as safe, proven or anti-aging results invite scrutiny, so we write with these limits in mind and the practice confirms final language with its counsel.

Advertising prescription drugs and compounded medications is subject to federal and state rules as well as each ad platform's own policies, which may restrict drug names and require certifications, so we build campaigns with these in mind and the practice should confirm the requirements with its counsel or compliance contact.

Testimonials, before-and-after photos and replies to reviews need written patient consent and must never confirm that someone is a patient or reveal health details, so we handle them with HIPAA requirements in mind and the practice confirms its policies with counsel.

family-practice.h1: Marketing for family practice and primary care
family-practice.lead: A primary care practice runs on full schedules and insurance panels, and many are now adding cash services such as aesthetics or weight loss. We market both sides without making your practice look like two different businesses.

primary care doctor who does botox

challenges.d: Insured patients looking for a family doctor and cash patients looking for weight loss or aesthetics search differently and decide differently. Your marketing has to speak to each without confusing the other or diluting the trust you have built as the family doctor.

Most of your patients have no idea you now offer a new service, and many are already buying it somewhere else. The fastest growth for a new service line often comes from your own panel, which means it depends on e-mail, text and what your staff says in the room.

Your phones are busy with refills, referrals and scheduling, so new-patient calls and cash-service inquiries wait or go unanswered. Marketing that produces more calls without a way to answer them only adds pressure on your staff.

care: Advertising for weight loss and hormone services often involves prescription drugs, and the rules on naming medications, describing compounded products and stating expected results are specific, so we write campaigns with these in mind and your practice should confirm the details with its counsel.
